questions.text: Walk me through a design in your portfolio where the final version differs sharply from your first concept. What changed it?
questions.rationale: The evolution story reveals process, feedback intake, and ego management.

questions.text: Tell me about a time user research contradicted your design instinct. What did you do?
questions.rationale: Evidence-over-instinct discipline, the mark of a mature designer.

questions.text: How do you design for a user you personally find frustrating or unlike yourself?
questions.rationale: Empathy as craft rather than sentiment; tests deliberate perspective-taking.

questions.text: Describe your handoff process to engineers. What do you include that prevents the most rework?
questions.rationale: Handoff craft is where design quality survives or dies in production.

questions.text: Tell me about a design decision you defended against stakeholder pushback and won. How?
questions.rationale: Persuasion grounded in evidence or principle rather than taste assertion.

questions.text: And tell me about one you defended and lost. Was the shipped version actually worse?
questions.rationale: The honest-loss follow-up tests whether conviction is calibrated.

questions.text: What kind of design work makes you lose track of time?
questions.rationale: Genuine craft energy located specifically within the discipline.

questions.text: Walk me through how you approach accessibility in your work. Give a specific decision from a recent project.
questions.rationale: Accessibility as practiced habit versus checklist afterthought.

questions.text: Describe a time you simplified a flow that had grown complicated. What did you cut and who objected?
questions.rationale: Simplification with named resistance shows both craft and courage.

questions.text: How do you use a design system without letting it flatten the product's character?
questions.rationale: System-versus-soul tension; tests sophistication about consistency's limits.

questions.text: Tell me about the most useful design critique you have received. What made it useful?
questions.rationale: Critique receptivity with articulated understanding of good feedback.

questions.text: How do you run a critique so that junior designers actually speak?
questions.rationale: Psychological safety as facilitation craft, tested concretely.

questions.text: Describe designing something under a deadline that did not allow research. What did you do instead?
questions.rationale: Rigor under constraint: proxies, heuristics, and honest risk labeling.

questions.text: Walk me through your favorite empty state you have designed. Why did it deserve that attention?
questions.rationale: Care for edge states signals product thinking beyond happy-path mockups.

questions.text: Tell me about working with a PM whose priorities kept shifting. How did you protect design quality?
questions.rationale: Quality defense inside realistic organizational churn.

questions.text: What is your relationship with data in design decisions? Tell me about a time metrics and usability conflicted.
questions.rationale: Metric-usability conflicts expose the candidate's real decision hierarchy.

questions.text: Describe your process from a vague brief to a first concept. What do you make first?
questions.rationale: Ambiguity-to-artifact process, the daily beginning of design work.

questions.text: Tell me about designing for mobile and desktop simultaneously. What broke and how did you resolve it?
questions.rationale: Responsive design judgment through a concrete breakage story.

questions.text: How do you know when a design is done enough to ship?
questions.rationale: Perfectionism calibration; the shipping threshold reveals pragmatism.

questions.text: What product's design do you consider quietly excellent, and what specific choice earns that?
questions.rationale: Taste with specificity; quiet excellence framing filters trend-chasing answers.

questions.text: Describe a time you tested a prototype with real users. What did you change based on round one?
questions.rationale: Prototype-test-iterate loop, evidenced with an actual change.

questions.text: Tell me about collaborating with a designer whose style differed sharply from yours.
questions.rationale: Style pluralism and collaboration over aesthetic territorialism.

questions.text: How do you present design work to executives? What do you show first?
questions.rationale: Executive communication as sequencing craft; the first-slide choice is telling.

questions.text: Walk me through your typography and hierarchy decisions on a recent screen. Why those choices?
questions.rationale: Micro-craft articulacy; strong designers can narrate their smallest decisions.

questions.text: As a design lead, how do you review work without redesigning it yourself? Give an example.
questions.rationale: The delegation-versus-takeover discipline that makes or breaks design leads.

questions.text: Tell me about growing a designer who was technically strong but struggled with communication.
questions.rationale: Developing the non-craft half of a designer; common and hard.

questions.text: What does design owe the business, and what does the business owe design?
questions.rationale: Mutual-obligation framing reveals maturity about design's organizational role.

questions.text: Describe a time you advocated for the user against a revenue-driven decision. How far did you push?
questions.rationale: User advocacy with a calibration probe on how conflict was navigated.

questions.text: What motivates you to keep designing when a project enters its tedious final ten percent?
questions.rationale: Finishing energy; many portfolios show starts, few show finish discipline.

questions.text: Tell me about a piece of feedback on your portfolio you disagreed with today. Argue with it.
questions.rationale: Live conviction testing; invites the candidate to reason under mild challenge.
